Incentive Delay Task

description.value: Participants viewed predictive erotic or monetary cues, performed a target discrimination, and then viewed reward outcomes when responses were correct and fast.

spans.text: Subjects first saw a cue informing them about the type (pictogram with a $ or a woman), magnitude (size of pictogram), and probability (pie chart) of an upcoming reward.
The target was either a triangle (left button press required) or a square (right button press required).

instructions.value: Participants viewed cues indicating reward type, magnitude, and probability, waited through an anticipation period, then identified a triangle or square by pressing the corresponding button within 1 second. Correct and sufficiently fast responses allowed presentation of the outcome; participants rated hedonic value from 1 (do not like it) to 9 (like it very much).

spans.text: Following this anticipation phase, participants had to perform a target discrimination task within 1 s.

stimuli.value: Cues depicting a dollar sign or a woman, with cue size indicating reward magnitude and a pie chart indicating 25%, 50%, or 75% probability. Monetary outcomes were gains of 1–3 PLN or 6–8 PLN; erotic outcomes were lingerie/swimsuit or explicit sexual images. Control trials used an empty circle and scrambled pictures.

spans.text: Both monetary and erotic cues provided information about the magnitude and probability of reward.

value: Reaction time in the target discrimination task

spans.text: RTs were later used as an index of motivation.
